scenes.narration: Hello, little friends! If a big cat tried to catch you every single day, what would you do? Is there a way to know the cat is coming, so you can run away in time? Today, Huy Tells Tales will tell you a fable called Belling the Cat.

Long ago, in a small village by the river dike, behind a green bamboo hedge, there was a little house with a thatched roof and mud walls. Under the dish cupboard, behind some big rice jars, a whole family of mice lived. Little Mouse (happily): "Mama, what are we going to eat today?" Mother Mouse (laughing): "In a little while, we will go out to the yard and pick up some fallen grains of rice."

But there was also Tabby Cat in that house. She had striped fur, bright eyes, and a long tail that swished from side to side. Tabby Cat (laughing): "Meow, meow! Tonight I will take another stroll around the kitchen and see what I find."

The cat walked very softly, because her claws were tucked away inside her soft paws. She liked to hunt in the evening, and her eyes could see well even in the dark. Often, before the mice heard a thing, the cat was already right behind them.

One night, Fat Mouse sneaked out to the pot of cold rice. Suddenly, a striped shadow leaped toward him. Fat Mouse (scared): "Oh no, the cat! Run!" Fat Mouse rolled into a crack in the wall and escaped just in time.

The next day, Little Mouse went out to play near the baskets, and Tabby Cat almost pounced on him. Luckily, Mother Mouse pulled her child into the burrow in time. Little Mouse (crying): "Mama, I am so scared!" Mother Mouse (worried): "It is all right now, my good child. Mama is here."

Every night was the same. The whole mouse family lived in fear and worry. Grandfather Mouse, with his white whiskers, looked at his children and grandchildren and felt sad. Grandfather Mouse (sadly): "If this goes on, not one of us will dare to leave our burrow." Gray Mouse (worried): "Yesterday I was nearly caught too, by the rice pounder."

Grandfather Mouse (firmly): "Tomorrow night, the whole family will meet under the dish cupboard. We must find a way to deal with the cat!" The news spread to every nook and corner, from the burrow under the water jar to the cracks in the wall behind the kitchen.

The next night, the mouse family gathered. Grandfather Mouse sat in the best spot, on a torn piece of reed mat. The children and grandchildren sat around him in order. Tiny Mouse (happily): "Good evening, Grandfather." Grandfather Mouse (laughing): "Good evening, child. Please sit down."
Grandfather Mouse (firmly): "Tabby Cat keeps hunting us. If anyone has a good idea, speak up so the whole family can hear." All the mice began to whisper and chatter.

Fat Mouse (joyfully): "What if we dig a very deep burrow and hide underground, so the cat can never find us?" Mother Mouse (surprised): "But then what will we eat, Fat Mouse? All the rice is up here." Fat Mouse (sadly): "Oh, you are right. Then we would be very hungry."

Gray Mouse (shouting): "What if we all rush out and fight the cat!" But after saying it, Gray Mouse's legs shook and shook. The whole family looked at each other and shook their heads. Grandfather Mouse (sadly): "The cat is dozens of times bigger than we are. How could we ever beat her, child?"

Just then, Tiny Mouse, the smallest of all, suddenly raised his hand, his eyes shining. Tiny Mouse (joyfully): "I have an idea!" Grandfather Mouse (surprised): "Tell us, child. The whole family is listening."
Tiny Mouse (happily): "The other day, I saw the farmer's buffalo wearing a bronze bell. Wherever the buffalo went, the bell went jingle-jingle." All the mice perked up their ears to listen.
Tiny Mouse (proudly): "So let us tie a bell around the cat's neck! Wherever the cat goes, the bell will ring. When we hear the jingle-jingle, we can run away in time!"

The whole space under the cupboard filled with clapping. The little mice jumped up and down with joy. Little Mouse (shouting): "Wonderful! Wonderful!" Fat Mouse (laughing): "From now on, we can eat our fill and sleep soundly!"
Mother Mouse (joyfully): "So our children and grandchildren will be able to live in peace." Gray Mouse (proudly): "A young one from the Mouse family really is something special. So clever!"
Little Mouse (joyfully): "I saw a little bell lying outside the buffalo shed!" So a few mice ran out and worked hard to drag the bell back. The bell went jingle-jingle all along the way.

The bell was placed right in the middle of the space under the cupboard. Grandfather Mouse raised his hand, and the whole family waited quietly. Grandfather Mouse (firmly): "The plan is wonderful, and we have the bell. But now, who will go and tie the bell around the cat's neck?"

Suddenly the whole space under the cupboard went completely silent. Only the crickets could be heard out in the yard. The mice looked at one another, and nobody said a word. Little Mouse (worried): "Mama, why is everyone so quiet?"

Grandfather Mouse (happily): "Fat Mouse, you are the biggest and strongest in the family. Will you go?" Fat Mouse (scared): "Oh, Grandfather, I am too fat and I run too slowly. The cat would catch me first!"
Fat Mouse (tired): "Ouch, all of a sudden my tummy hurts so much. Please let me go home first!" Then Fat Mouse held his tummy and scurried quickly into the crack in the wall.

Grandfather Mouse (sadly): "What about Mother Mouse and little Út?" Mother Mouse (worried): "I must look after my little one. I cannot possibly go." Mother Mouse led Little Mouse back into the shadows behind the water jar.

Grandfather Mouse (surprised): "Gray Mouse, you just said we should rush out and fight the cat, didn't you?" Gray Mouse (scared): "Yes, but I have to guard the entrance of the burrow. If nobody guards it, it will be very dangerous!" Gray Mouse ran off as he spoke. One by one, the other mice found excuses and slipped away too.

Grandfather Mouse (sadly): "And you, Tiny Mouse, who thought of the best idea?" Tiny Mouse (scared): "Oh, I am only good at thinking. I am so tiny, I could never reach the cat's neck." Then Tiny Mouse also bowed his head and tiptoed into the crack in the wall.
Now only Grandfather Mouse was left, sitting alone beside the bronze bell. Grandfather Mouse (sadly): "The bell is here, the good plan is here, and yet nobody dares to do it."

On the pile of straw in the corner of the kitchen, Tabby Cat stretched and pricked up her ears to listen. Tabby Cat (surprised): "Meow, what is that sound under the cupboard?" Grandfather Mouse (scared): "The cat is coming! The cat is coming!" Grandfather Mouse dashed into his burrow. The bell was left lying on the dirt floor.

Tabby Cat walked over and poked the bell with her paw. The bell went jingle-jingle and rolled into a corner of the kitchen. Tabby Cat (laughing): "What are those mice up to now? Oh well, I will go back to sleep."

The next morning, the sun rose behind the bamboo hedge. Grandfather Mouse called his children and grandchildren to gather around him. Little Mouse (sadly): "Grandfather, so Tiny Mouse's plan cannot be used after all?"
Grandfather Mouse (sadly): "My dear children, saying is easy, but doing is hard." Grandfather Mouse (firmly): "No matter how good a plan is, if nobody can do it, it is worth nothing."
Tiny Mouse (sadly): "I understand now. Next time I will think of plans that we can really do." Fat Mouse (sadly): "I am sorry too, Grandfather, for using a tummy ache as an excuse yesterday."

From then on, the story of the mouse family was passed down by grandparents to their grandchildren. Even today, when someone comes up with a plan that sounds good but that nobody can carry out, people say it is like belling the cat. Just like The Blind Men and the Elephant or The Plow Carved by the Roadside, the lesson of this story has become a well-known saying.

Little friends, having a good idea is wonderful. But what matters even more is daring to do it, and only promising what we can really do. If you liked today's story, please ask your parents to subscribe to the channel Huy Kể Chuyện, so you can hear many more good stories. See you next time!
